quarterly_data.signal: Q1 (Apr-Jun 2026) record highs across the board: revenue JPY 1,767.1 billion (QoQ +76.2%, YoY +415.5%, vs guidance JPY 1,750 billion), non-GAAP gross profit JPY 1,405.5 billion (gross margin 80%, 82% excluding JV-related items), non-GAAP operating profit JPY 1,326.2 billion (margin 75%, QoQ 2.2x, YoY +2,833.2%) - one quarter already exceeded all of FY2025's JPY 876.2 billion OP. Non-GAAP net income JPY 887 billion (margin 50.2%, YoY +4,692.5%), non-GAAP EBITDA JPY 1,402.1 billion (margin 79.3%), non-GAAP EPS JPY 1,621.81. Like-for-like and blended ASP both increased by 70% QoQ with low-single-digit shipment volume growth. Core free cash flow (new KPI) JPY 827.2 billion; operating cash flow JPY 866.3 billion. Senior loan fully repaid (JPY 407.5 billion) achieving a NET CASH position; cash and equivalents a record JPY 791.0 billion; equity ratio 51%, D/E ratio now negative 8%.

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY guidance (single-number, no longer a range): revenue JPY 2,390.0 billion (QoQ +35%), non-GAAP operating profit JPY 1,900 billion (margin 79.9%, QoQ +43.3%), non-GAAP profit before tax JPY 1,880.0 billion (new disclosure item), non-GAAP net income JPY 1,280 billion (margin 53.6%, QoQ +44.3%), non-GAAP EPS JPY 2,335.70; FX assumption JPY 162/USD (sensitivity: JPY 1 move = JPY 14 billion revenue / JPY 13 billion OP per quarter). About 70% of the expected Q2 growth comes from higher ASP, with continued volume growth; data center and enterprise demand drives the volume, smartphone stable with seasonality, PC may be slightly weaker. Third and fourth quarters: production plan remains intact and results are expected to follow the strong demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 guide: revenue JPY 2,390.0 billion (+35% QoQ), OP JPY 1,900 billion (79.9% margin), net income JPY 1,280 billion; ~70% of growth from ASP

quarterly_data.signal: NAND market view: growth in AI demand is driving the NAND market with data centers and enterprise applications leading; agentic AI applications are a key growth driver, impacting even demand for traditional servers. Smartphone NAND demand expected flat vs calendar 2025 (low-priced model shipments declining, high-end steady with rising storage capacity); PC shipments to decrease on rising BOM costs (NAND slightly down). Calendar 2026 NAND market bit growth anticipated in the high teens percentage range, in line with Kioxia's own bit growth; for calendar 2027 demand is forecast to EXCEED supply. QLC NAND SSD replacing nearline HDD in data centers is an opportunity, though the transition may be slower than expected while the market is skewed toward high-end pricing.
quarterly_data.figure: CY2026 NAND bit growth high teens %; CY2027 demand to exceed supply

quarterly_data.signal: By application: SSD and storage revenue JPY 1,174.7 billion (QoQ +95.7%, YoY +440.3%, record) - data center/enterprise now accounts for over 60% of the segment (PC less than 40%), driven by growing AI server demand with record volume and record revenue; the Q1 SSD/storage quarter alone is close to all of FY2025's JPY 1,362.6 billion. Smart devices revenue JPY 525.7 billion (QoQ +55.8%, YoY +565.1%, record, price-driven); others JPY 66.7 billion. BiCS8 now exceeds 50% of entire production. A portion of shipment volume slipped from Q1 into Q2 (delivery timing at quarter end, not significant in gigabytes).
quarterly_data.figure: SSD & storage revenue JPY 1,174.7 billion (+95.7% QoQ, +440.3% YoY); data center/enterprise >60% of segment; BiCS8 >50% of production

quarterly_data.signal: Long-term agreements (LTAs) with major customers including hyperscalers: Kioxia aims for 50% of total shipment volume to be covered by LTA by calendar year 2028 and is 'pretty much on track' toward that goal. Three aims: visualize long-term demand, underpin growth investment, and deepen future-looking business/technology engagement with enterprise and hyperscaler key players. Terms are bespoke per customer (NDA-bound); discussions currently cover 2027 to 2028, and most recently customers are asking for even longer-term frameworks, which Kioxia is proactively engaging on.
quarterly_data.figure: Target: 50% of shipment volume under LTA by 2028 - on track

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and technology roadmap: multi-site production at Yokkaichi (one of the world's largest flash memory bases, leading-edge R&D) and Kitakami; the K2 fab at Kitakami began operation in September 2025 and began production of the 10th generation BiCS FLASH this year. Capex plan: average JPY 470 billion annually from FY2026 to FY2028 (JPY 450 billion this year), flexible to market change and fully covered by cash flow. R&D about JPY 200 billion for the full year, concentrated on BiCS 10/BiCS 11 and AI inference SSDs (super high IOPS SSD for inference servers); UFS 5.0 new high-speed standard for edge AI / on-device AI announced. Strategy: not pursuing market share through aggressive investment - pursuing quality and profitability via higher sequential speed, energy efficiency and product quality.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex average JPY 470 billion/year FY2026-FY2028 (JPY 450 billion this year); R&D ~JPY 200 billion; BiCS10 in production at Kitakami K2, BiCS11 and AI inference SSD in development

quarterly_data.signal: Capital returns and investments: share buyback of up to 30 million shares (5.5% of shares outstanding), maximum JPY 800 billion, acquisition period August 3rd to October 30th 2026 - timed to the lower share price to improve EPS; 3-for-1 stock split effective October 1st to broaden the investor base; dividend under discussion for the second half. Policy: about 50% of excess free cash flow (after capex, R&D, HR investment and working capital) allocated to shareholder return. Also invested JPY 78.2 billion to acquire equity in Taiwanese Nanya (booked in investment cash flow); building strategic DRAM inventory (inventories up JPY 25.5 billion, ~100 days).
quarterly_data.figure: Buyback max JPY 800 billion (30 million shares, 5.5%); 3-for-1 split; JPY 78.2 billion Nanya equity investment
